content: Do not take valsartan if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as valsartan can cause harm to the developing fetus. It is also used to manage heart failure in patients who cannot tolerate angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin II receptor antagonists. It works by blocking the effects of certain chemicals that constrict blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Valsartan is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For heart failure, it is usually taken twice daily, also with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take valsartan exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less than the recommended dose or take it more frequently than directed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting valsartan, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to valsartan or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril), beta blockers (e.g., atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), or diuretics (water pills). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, or if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of valsartan, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Valsartan may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: Dizziness Headache Fatigue Diarrhea Stomach pain Back pain Joint pain Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Hoarseness Difficulty breathing or swallowing Fainting If you notice any unusual symptoms while taking valsartan, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store valsartan in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness, fainting, or a rapid or pounding heartbeat. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory to monitor your response to valsartan. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Valsartan is sold under the brand name Diovan®. Combination products containing valsartan and hydrochlorothiazide are marketed as Diovan® HCT.
